title: Allu Arjun Faces the Court From a Mumbai Film Set. The Pushpa 2 Stampede Case Catches Up With the Pan-India Star.
excerpt: Named 'Accused No. 11' over the death that shadowed his biggest hit, the Telugu superstar appeared virtually before Hyderabad's Nampally Court — and the hearing was deferred again.
body:
He's played a fearless rebel who stares down syndicates and a coolie who turns into a kingdom's most wanted man. But on Monday, Allu Arjun — the biggest pan-Indian star Telugu cinema has produced — faced a far less cinematic frame: a courtroom, accessed by video link, from a shooting floor in Mumbai.

The man the world knows as Pushpa appeared virtually before Hyderabad's Nampally Court in connection with the Sandhya Theatre stampede — the tragedy that turned the triumphant December 2024 release of *Pushpa 2: The Rule* into one of Indian cinema's darkest footnotes. The court had summoned 19 of the 23 people named in the chargesheet to appear in person on June 22. Allu Arjun, listed as accused number 11, sought permission to join by video conferencing, citing his ongoing film shoot. The court allowed it — and then deferred the hearing.

What actually happened that night

https://x.com/ANI/status/2068977598332588328

To understand the gravity, you have to go back to December 4, 2024. A benefit show of *Pushpa 2* was organised at the Sandhya Theatre in Hyderabad, and the city's fan culture — that gloriously unhinged devotion South Indian cinema inspires — did what it does. A crowd swelled far beyond the venue's capacity as word spread that the star himself had arrived.

He had. According to the police investigation, Allu Arjun reached the theatre with his family to watch the film, and fans surged toward the entry gate to catch a glimpse of him. The pressure became unmanageable. Security arrangements, the chargesheet alleges, collapsed entirely.

> "Her young son, Sri Teja, was critically injured — admitted in a semi-conscious state, later requiring prolonged ventilator support amid respiratory and neurological complications."

In the chaos, a woman named Revathi lost her life. Her young son, Sri Teja, was critically injured — admitted in a semi-conscious state, later requiring prolonged ventilator support amid respiratory and neurological complications. After nearly five months of intensive care, he was discharged in April 2025 and moved to a rehabilitation facility. It is the human cost that no box-office number can ever offset, and it sits at the centre of this case.

A star, briefly, behind bars

![Mumbai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2b/Mumbai_Bandra-Worli_Sea_Link.jpg)

What followed was extraordinary even by the standards of Indian celebrity. On December 13, 2024, Allu Arjun was arrested over the incident and produced before a local court, which sent him to 14-day judicial custody. He spent a night at Chanchalguda Central Jail before the Telangana High Court granted him interim bail on a personal bond of ₹50,000. In all, the actor was in custody for roughly 18 hours — but the image of one of the country's most adored stars walking out of a central jail at dawn is not one his fans will forget.

> "This was all an accident. I had gone to the cinema hall with my family to watch a movie. I have no direct connection with this incident. I am completely with the woman's family, and I will help them in any way I can." — Allu Arjun, after his release

The chargesheet places primary blame on the theatre management — named as accused 1 through 10 — alleging negligence by officials, security staff, and event-management personnel. Allu Arjun's defence has consistently held that he bears no direct responsibility for crowd control outside a venue he was simply attending.

The family's quiet repair

Away from the legal machinery, there's been a parallel story of contrition. Producer Allu Aravind, the actor's father, announced ₹2 crore in assistance to Revathi's bereaved family. The Allu family — including Aravind and the actor's wife Sneha Reddy — reportedly visited Sri Teja, enquired after his recovery, and pledged to cover the educational expenses of his younger sister. Gestures, of course, cannot undo a death. But they signal a family acutely aware that this stain runs deeper than any PR cycle.

Why the diaspora should care

For NRI fans who turned *Pushpa 2* into a global event — packing out theatres in New Jersey, London, and Toronto, queuing at midnight for first-day-first-show — this case is a sobering coda to the euphoria. It has forced a long-overdue industry conversation about the lethal underside of fan frenzy: the benefit shows, the star appearances, the crowd surges that no one polices until someone dies.

*Pushpa 2* remains available to stream, and Allu Arjun's next, the long-gestating Atlee sci-fi spectacle reportedly titled *AA22xA6*, keeps him firmly at the top of the pan-Indian pile. But the proceedings at Nampally will grind on, hearing by hearing, a reminder that even the most untouchable stardom answers, eventually, to a courtroom.

What's next

With the hearing deferred, the case moves to its next date, and the 19 summoned accused remain bound to the court's process. Allu Arjun's legal team has signalled it will continue to appear — virtually or otherwise — as the matter proceeds. For now, the rebel star keeps shooting in Mumbai. The reckoning, however, is still in session.
